paragraphs: Children from Southport who need foster care are the responsibility of Sefton Council, which runs its own fostering service across the borough, including Southport and Bootle. Independent agencies such as the services shown above also care for children from the town.

Sefton has been clear that it needs more carers. At the start of 2025 it said more children were coming into care, its existing carers were almost full, and it aimed to approve 30 new fostering families that year. In May 2026, during Foster Care Fortnight, it said hundreds of carers already open their homes in Sefton but many more are urgently needed so each child can be matched with the right home, echoing The Fostering Network's warning that more carers are leaving than joining nationally.

The council says you can foster whether you are single, married, retired, employed or self-employed, and that what counts is offering a caring home. Fostering can last a night, a few months or several years, and Sefton recruits for full-time fostering as well as respite and emergency care. It says carers are paid for their skills on top of allowances and receive full training and support, and that you could welcome a child in as little as six months. Some of its experienced carers act as Foster Carer Advocates, talking to people at local events about what fostering is really like.

Southport is often where Sefton meets the public, with information evenings and stands in the town in recent years. Talk to the council and to two or three of the agencies above, and ask each about training, payments and support close to home.
